answer: Fresh identities start at the lotus stage, cheap but capped in influence, and only mature as organic attestations accumulate. Sybil resistance here uses stake-weighted identity: each agent locks a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and every attestation creates a ripple through the peer graph that raises or lowers that bond's required size. A mass of fake agents must post real capital and sustain genuine peer confirmations, so the economic tide turns against attackers: forging identities costs more than legitimate participation earns.
